newsitem.title: USA: Chrysler reports record Q1 profits as workers strike.
newsitem.headline: Chrysler reports record Q1 profits as workers strike.

text.p: Hours after workers struck a key Chrysler Corp. engine plant on Thursday, the automaker reported record first-quarter profits of $1.029 billion, an increase of 2.4 percent from the $1.005 billion it earned a year ago.

Chrysler said its retail incentives rose for the quarter, but those costs were offset by higher production, including more of the profitable light-truck models that could be affected by a prolonged walkout at the company's Mound Road engine plant in Detroit.

Chrysler said its first-quarter fully diluted earnings per share rose to $1.45, slightly beating the consensus analyst estimate of $1.43, according to First Call Corp., which tracks Wall Street earnings estimates. A year ago, Chrysler's profits were equal to $1.30 a share, fully diluted.
Chrysler finished the first quarter with total revenues of $16.12 billion, up from $14.96 billion. Worldwide factory unit shipments to dealers increased to 781,239 from 753,176.
The No. 3 U.S. automaker spent an average of $705 on retail incentives in the quarter, up from $640 a year ago.

"With the steady growth of the U.S. economy and the continued strength of Chrysler's product lineup, we were successful in maintaining our pace at near-record first-quarter sales levels," Chrysler Chairman Robert Eaton said in a statement accompanying the results.
Although the weak Japanese yen and new products from Japanese automakers has boosted their competitiveness, Eaton said the company remains optimistic about the spring selling season.
Shortly after midnight Wednesday, about 1,800 United Auto Workers union members at the engine plant went on strike over outsourcing issues.

Most of the engines built at Mound Road are used in Chrysler's Dodge Ram and Dakota pickup trucks. They include a 3.9-litre V-6, the 5.2-litre and 5.9-litre V-8s and a monster 8-litre V-10 used in the heaviest versions of the Ram.
The 5.2-litre V8 also is a popular option in the Jeep Grand Cherokee sport utility vehicle.
